reviews.title: Rough start but good ending
reviews.comment: The first motherboard box arrived in what appeared to be perfect condition. However upon opening the package I noticed that the processor socket add a slight indent on one or two of the pins. This made me a bit leery but I went ahead and installed the processor (my first socket 1851 build). It gave all kind of issues. I finally decided to have it replaced and the replacement worked good --- overall very happy with the this motherboard packaged with the Intel Ultra 5, G. SKILL Ripjaws S5 Series DDR5 RAM 32GB (2x16GB) 6400MT/s CL32-39-39-102 1.40V Desktop Computer Memory UDIMM.

reviews.title: It's a good board, but the bios software could be a lot better
reviews.comment: For a Micro-ATX board, the GIGABYTE B860M Gaming X has a surprisingly thoughtful layout. The primary GPU slot is positioned well, though—as with most mATX boards—you’ll need to be strategic with cable management to ensure the video card doesn't choke your airflow. The RAM slots and the primary NVMe slot were easy to access, and I really appreciated that the pin-outs were clearly labeled on the PCB, making the front-panel header setup a breeze. The BIOS Experience: This is where things got "interesting." If you are migrating an older drive, be aware that Gigabyte has moved away from Legacy Mode/CSM. I hot-swapped my existing NVMe and had a nightmare getting the board to detect it initially, despite it being formatted correctly. The BIOS GUI itself feels clunky and unintuitive compared to previous generations. I found myself relying heavily on the "Search" function just to find basic settings. If you’ve used Gigabyte for years, be prepared for a learning curve with this new interface. Summary: The hardware is reliable and the build quality is there, but the software side feels like a step backward in terms of user-friendliness. Great for a fresh Windows 11 install, but a bit of a headache for those carrying over older hardware.
